screening_decisions.reason: This is a randomised trial comparing indomethacin (a COX inhibitor) with terbutaline for tocolysis in women with preterm labour at 26-32 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, COX inhibitor used for tocolysis, women in preterm labour, within 20-36 weeks gestation.

This is an observational pharmacokinetic study examining placental transfer of indomethacin, not a randomised trial. Indomethacin was administered before cordocenteses undertaken for standard indications, not for tocolysis. Does not meet the RCT design criterion nor the tocolysis indication criterion.

This is a Cochrane systematic review about magnesium sulphate for fetal neuroprotection, not a primary randomised trial. It does not involve COX inhibitors as the intervention. Does not meet the RCT design criterion nor the COX inhibitor intervention criterion.

This is a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial comparing celecoxib (a COX-2 selective inhibitor) with indomethacin (a non-selective COX inhibitor) for treatment of preterm labour at 24-34 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, COX inhibitors used for tocolysis, women in preterm labour, within 20-36 weeks gestation.

This is a randomised, double-blind trial comparing sulindac (a COX inhibitor) with terbutaline for management of preterm labour at approximately 32 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, COX inhibitor used for tocolysis, women in preterm labour, within 20-36 weeks gestation.

This is a systematic review/meta-analysis about progestational agents for preterm labour, not a primary randomised trial. It does not involve COX inhibitors as the intervention. Does not meet the RCT design criterion nor the COX inhibitor intervention criterion.

This is a methodological paper comparing statistical analysis methods for trials involving multiple pregnancies. It is not a clinical trial of any intervention, and does not involve COX inhibitors or tocolysis. Does not meet the RCT design criterion nor the COX inhibitor intervention criterion.

This is a prospective, double-blind randomised trial comparing ritodrine plus indomethacin (a COX inhibitor) versus ritodrine plus placebo for threatened preterm labour. Meets selection criteria: RCT design, COX inhibitor used for tocolysis, women in preterm labour. Gestational age not explicitly stated but implied to be preterm.

This is a randomised, double-blind, double-dummy trial comparing indomethacin (a COX inhibitor) with nylidrin for imminent preterm labour at 25-34 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, COX inhibitor used for tocolysis, women in preterm labour, within 20-36 weeks gestation.

This is a matched case-control study (57 indomethacin-exposed infants matched with 57 unexposed infants), not a randomised trial. While it examines neonatal outcomes after indomethacin for preterm labour, it does not meet the RCT design criterion.

This is a methodological paper comparing statistical analysis methods (logistic regression, GEEs, mixed effects models) for trials involving multiple births. It is not a clinical trial of any intervention, and does not involve COX inhibitors or tocolysis. Does not meet the RCT design criterion nor the COX inhibitor intervention criterion.

This is a randomised trial of rofecoxib (COX-2 selective inhibitor) for prophylactic prevention of preterm delivery in women at high risk. However, treatment was administered from 16 to 32 weeks gestation, starting at 16 weeks which is below the 20-week lower limit specified in the selection criteria. Additionally, this is prophylactic use in women at high risk, not treatment of women actively in preterm labour. Excluded based on gestational age criterion (starts at 16 weeks) and indication (prophylaxis vs. active tocolysis).

This is a randomised, double-masked trial comparing indomethacin (a COX inhibitor) with placebo for prophylactic tocolysis in women with PPROM at 24-31 weeks gestation. While the women have PPROM rather than active preterm labour, indomethacin is used as a tocolytic agent. Meets selection criteria: RCT design, COX inhibitor used for tocolysis, within 20-36 weeks gestation. Included conservatively as the intervention is tocolysis with a COX inhibitor.

This is a randomised trial comparing indomethacin with sulindac (both COX inhibitors) for treatment of refractory preterm labour at 29-30 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, COX inhibitors used for tocolysis, women in preterm labour, within 20-36 weeks gestation.

This is a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial examining the effects of indomethacin (a COX inhibitor) and terbutaline on fetal breathing and body movements in women at 26-32 weeks gestation. While the women did not have active preterm labour, indomethacin was administered as a tocolytic agent. Meets selection criteria: RCT design, COX inhibitor used as tocolytic, within 20-36 weeks gestation. Included conservatively.

This is a prospective randomised double-blind trial comparing indomethacin (a COX inhibitor) with placebo for inhibition of premature labour. Meets selection criteria: RCT design, COX inhibitor used for tocolysis, women in preterm labour. Gestational age not explicitly stated but implied to be preterm.

This is a randomised trial comparing ketorolac (a COX inhibitor) with magnesium sulfate for arrest of preterm labour at ≤32 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, COX inhibitor used for tocolysis, women in preterm labour, within 20-36 weeks gestation.

This is a systematic review and network meta-analysis of tocolytic therapy for preterm delivery, not a primary randomised trial. While it includes prostaglandin inhibitors (COX inhibitors) as one drug class, it is a secondary synthesis of evidence, not a primary RCT. Does not meet the RCT design criterion.

This is a Cochrane systematic review about betamimetics for inhibiting preterm labour, not a primary randomised trial. It does not involve COX inhibitors as the intervention. Does not meet the RCT design criterion nor the COX inhibitor intervention criterion.

This is a randomised prospective trial comparing indomethacin (a COX inhibitor) with ritodrine for long-term treatment of preterm labour at 23-34 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, COX inhibitor used for tocolysis, women in preterm labour, within 20-36 weeks gestation.
This is an in vitro animal experimental study using pregnant Wistar rat myometrial strips, not a randomised trial in human women. Does not meet the study design criterion.

Randomised placebo-controlled trial of indomethacin (COX inhibitor) vs placebo in women in preterm labour between 23-30 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, COX inhibitor used for tocolysis, correct gestational age range.

Randomized trial comparing celecoxib (COX-2 selective inhibitor) vs magnesium sulfate in women with preterm labour between 24-34 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, COX inhibitor used for tocolysis, correct gestational age range.
This is a historical review article discussing the development and use of prostaglandin synthesis inhibitors over time. Not a randomised trial. Does not meet the study design criterion.

Randomized double-blind study of indomethacin (COX inhibitor) vs terbutaline vs placebo in patients at 26-32 weeks gestation. While the primary outcome is umbilical artery velocimetry rather than clinical outcomes, this is an RCT using COX inhibitors for tocolysis in the correct population. Conservative approach favors inclusion.
Basic science laboratory study examining COX-1 and COX-2 expression in human myometrium using RT-PCR and Western blotting. Not a randomised trial. Does not meet the study design criterion.

Randomized double-blind clinical trial where indomethacin (COX inhibitor) was administered as adjunctive therapy with magnesium sulfate for tocolysis in women with preterm labour (mean 30.1 weeks). Meets selection criteria: RCT design, COX inhibitor used for tocolysis, correct gestational age range.
This is a Cochrane systematic review about antenatal corticosteroids, not a randomised trial of COX inhibitors. Does not meet the intervention or study design criteria.

Retrospective review of neonatal intensive care patient data warehouse. Not a randomised trial. While indomethacin use is mentioned as a risk factor, this is not an interventional study of COX inhibitors for tocolysis.

Comparative observational study examining progesterone levels in women treated with ritodrin vs indomethacin. No randomization described; women were assigned to treatment groups but not randomly allocated. Does not meet the RCT criterion.

Randomized allocation of women in preterm labour (26-33 weeks) to receive indomethacin (COX inhibitor) or nylidrin. While the primary outcome is CRH levels, this is an RCT using COX inhibitors for tocolysis in the correct population. Conservative approach favors inclusion.
Structured review of literature on economic consequences of preterm birth. Not a randomised trial. Does not meet the study design criterion.
Qualitative naturalistic inquiry using grounded-theory techniques interviewing parents about their experiences. Not a randomised trial. Does not meet the study design criterion.

While women received indomethacin or nylidrin treatment, the abstract does not describe randomization ('Women with preterm labor were treated with indomethacin (12 women) or nylidrin (13 women)'). Without explicit randomization, cannot confirm RCT status. Excluded conservatively.
Retrospective cohort study examining delivery site and mortality outcomes. Not a randomised trial. Does not meet the study design criterion.
Cochrane systematic review about calcium channel blockers, not a randomised trial of COX inhibitors. Does not meet the intervention or study design criteria.

Randomized double-blind trial of mefenamic acid (non-selective COX inhibitor) vs placebo in women at risk of premature delivery. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, COX inhibitor used for tocolysis/prevention of preterm labour.

Randomized study comparing indomethacin vs sulindac (both COX inhibitors) in pregnancies with threatened premature labour between 28-32 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, COX inhibitors used for tocolysis, correct gestational age range.

Comparative trial including indomethacin (COX inhibitor) for preterm labour. While randomization is not explicitly stated, the term 'comparative trial' suggests controlled comparison. Conservative approach favors inclusion given COX inhibitor use for tocolysis.

Randomized trial of indomethacin (COX inhibitor) vs magnesium sulfate in patients with preterm labour at <30 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, COX inhibitor used for tocolysis, correct gestational age range.

This study describes an observational series of 297 women treated with indomethacin, not a randomized controlled trial. The abstract states 'The effect of indomethacin...was evaluated in a series of 297 women' without mentioning randomization.
This is a meta-analysis/systematic review, not a primary randomized trial. The methods state 'A systematic review was conducted' analyzing 8 studies on NSAID use and ductal closure.
This is an in vitro laboratory study using serum-free organ culture of human mid-gestation intestinal tissue, not a clinical trial involving pregnant women receiving tocolysis.

This is a randomized controlled trial where women at risk of premature delivery were randomly assigned to receive mefenamic acid (a non-selective COX inhibitor/NSAID) or placebo in a double-blind fashion. Mefenamic acid is a COX inhibitor used for tocolysis.
This is a Cochrane systematic review about combination tocolytic agents, not a primary randomized trial. It does not focus specifically on COX inhibitors.
This is an epidemiological review paper describing causes and risk factors of preterm birth. It is not a randomized trial and does not involve any intervention with COX inhibitors.
This is a meta-analysis of 12 randomized trials assessing maintenance tocolytic therapy. It is a secondary analysis, not a primary randomized trial, and does not specifically focus on COX inhibitors.

This is a randomized controlled trial where women in acute preterm labor were randomized to receive indomethacin (a COX inhibitor), magnesium sulfate, or nifedipine. Average gestational age at randomization was 28.6 weeks (within 20-36 week range). Indomethacin is a non-selective COX inhibitor used for tocolysis.
This is a community-based cohort study following up infants born preterm in Malawi. It is observational, not a randomized trial, and does not involve COX inhibitor tocolysis as an intervention.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing indomethacin (a COX inhibitor) versus magnesium sulfate for management of preterm labor in pregnancies <32 weeks gestation. Patients were randomized by sealed envelopes.
This is a matched retrospective cohort study, not a randomized trial. The abstract states it examined 'infants born to 72 mothers' in a 'matched retrospective cohort study' design.
This is a Cochrane systematic review about nitric oxide donors for preterm labour, not a primary randomized trial. It does not focus on COX inhibitors.
This is a review article presenting 'a review of the literature and the experience at our institution' on prostaglandin synthetase inhibitors. It is not a randomized trial.

This is a population-based perinatal database study analyzing temporal trends in preterm birth in Scotland from 1980-2004. It is observational, not a randomized trial, and does not involve COX inhibitor intervention.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing oral rofecoxib (a COX-2 selective inhibitor) with intravenous magnesium sulfate for arresting preterm labor. Patients were between 22 and 34 weeks gestation (within 20-36 week range). Rofecoxib is a COX-2 selective inhibitor used for tocolysis.
This is a Cochrane systematic review about magnesium sulphate for preventing preterm birth, not a primary randomized trial. It does not focus on COX inhibitors.

This is a double-blind, double-dummy prospective randomized study comparing three COX inhibitors (indomethacin, sulindac, and nimesulide) for treatment of preterm labor. Subjects were at 28 to 32 weeks gestation (within 20-36 week range). All three drugs are COX inhibitors used for tocolysis.

This is a prospective, randomized, double-blind trial comparing indomethacin (a COX inhibitor) with placebo for treatment of premature labor. Indomethacin was significantly more effective than placebo in inhibiting premature labor.
